recentItems.title: Turns out, your group chat might be more powerful than you think. #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: Katie Paris quit her career in Washington, DC, to figure out how to make politics feel less like strangers shouting at each other and more like friends looking out for each other. In this practical talk, she reveals why conversations between real people can have a bigger impact on elections than anything millions of campaign dollars can buy.

recentItems.title: Inside Venezuela’s Uncertain Path to Freedom | Leopoldo López | TED
recentItems.description:
Activist Leopoldo López learned the true value of freedom in a solitary confinement cell, when someone else decided if he would eat or see sunlight. In this searching conversation, he explains why democracy is losing ground across the globe, the state of Venezuela's transition after Maduro's capture and the 2026 earthquakes — and why he founded the World Liberty Congress to unite activists in the fight against autocracies. (This conversation, hosted by TED's Whitney Pennington Rogers, was part of an exclusive TED Membership event. recentItems.title: How Would You Design Your Dream City? | James Rojas | TED
recentItems.description:
Urban planner James Rojas has led hundreds of workshops where participants creatively design their ideal communities with small objects — and he's noticed that people of every age, income and background build strikingly similar places. Through play and storytelling, he shows how we can use our childhood memories and imaginations to shape the places we live and love. (Recorded at Play@TED on May 14, 2026)

recentItems.title: Photographer Platon says empathy is the secret ingredient for finding a human connection. #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: With his art, photographer Platon seeks to strip away assumptions and leave viewers with a window into his subject's character, filling our eyes with wonder and curiosity. Sharing extraordinary stories of what it's like to photograph some of the world's most prominent figures -- from Michelle Obama and Pussy Riot to Vladimir Putin and Muhammad Ali -- Platon captures the disarming power of empathy and human connection.

recentItems.title: When a couple creates their own world together, love thrives #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: Social psychologist Eli J. Finkel has spent decades studying what makes partnerships successful. In a practical talk drawing on lessons from pop culture, he explores why so many of us struggle to be true to ourselves in our relationships — and what the happiest couples do differently.

recentItems.title: How People Are Using AI to Grieve, Love and Connect | Jennifer Cearns | TED
recentItems.description:
Many people fear AI is eroding our humanity, replacing real relationships with synthetic ones that leave us lonelier than ever. Digital anthropologist Jennifer Cearns believes the opposite may be true. After talking to hundreds of people who turn to AI for grief, love, friendship and more, she pokes holes in this familiar fear — and hints at what these strange new relationships can teach us about ourselves. (Recorded at TED2026 on April 16, 2026)

recentItems.title: AI Brain Fry Is Real. Here’s What Leaders Can Do | Julie Bedard | TED
recentItems.description:
Workers everywhere are quietly redesigning their jobs around AI, boosting productivity but also creating new kinds of problems. AI advisor Julie Bedard thinks she has a fix. She shares new research on three areas for leaders to focus on — including how to avoid "AI brain fry" — and why we need to shape this change rather than let it happen to us. (Recorded at TED@BCG on August 17, 2026)

recentItems.title: In a world of endless health advice, clarity and context might be the best prescription #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: Why does searching your symptoms online always leave you more frightened than before? As former chief medical officer of WebMD, physician John Whyte spent years believing more information meant better health — until he saw how too much of it was making people spiral. In a world of health influencers, algorithms and AI tools designed to keep you clicking, he reveals why clarity and context is a better prescription.

recentItems.title: I Can’t Speak. Here’s How I Get People to Listen | Jessica Irwin | TED
recentItems.description:
Jessica Irwin is many things: a photographer, artist, author, performer. She also happens to be nonverbal, born with cerebral palsy that affects the muscles she needs to talk. Speaking through a device that turns her typed words into speech, she gives a sharp, funny and urgent reminder that being unable to speak has nothing to do with intelligence — and shares a few easy ways anyone can better communicate with nonverbal people. (Recorded at TED2026 on April 16, 2026)

recentItems.title: We’re all less cult-proof than we would like to think #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: Nobody joins a cult on purpose, says Sarah Edmondson, a former member of the infamous Nxivm cult and one of the three whistleblowers that led to its downfall. She explains how she got ensnared in this highly manipulative group — and then escaped it — and shares red flags to help you distinguish between a cult and a safe community.
